CONVENTION SUPPLEMENT.
APRIL, 1883.
THE SEMI-CENTENNIAL CONVENTION.
The Fiftieth Convention of the Psi Upsilon Frater
nity will be held at Albany, N. Y., May 23d, 24th,
and 25th.
When the Committee of Arrangements for the com
memoration of the Semi-Oentennial Anniversary of
the Fraternity entered upon their labors, all prelim
inaries were settled for holding the exercises at Sche
nectady. But, as the work progressed, the fact
became evident that satisfactory preparations could
not be made for a celebration in Sclieneotady which
would be fitting for such an illustrious occasion.
Albany, seventeen miles distant, combining unexcelled
hotel accommodations, -with a central railroad pssition,
was suggested by some of the neighboring Chapters
and many of the Alumni as a desirable place. Con
sidering its central location, the Committee selected
Albany as the place for holding the exercises.
AU arrangements are advancing rapidly, and every
indication points to a gathering and celebration which
will'fitly crown the half-oentury existence of our be
loved Fraternity. Inasmuch as each day will be
marked with some interesting exercises, and the busi
ness meetings will be of a highly important character,
it is very desirable that the brothers make arrange
ments for an early arrival at Albany. A detailed ac
count of the several exercises of the occasion is pre
sented in the following pages.
OBJECT OF THE SUPPLEMENT.
It has been customary heretofore, a few weeks pre
vious to the time of the annual convention of Psi Up
silon, to send cards to the Alumni and active members
of the Fraternity, briefly stating the date and most
important facts in regard to the event. It was deemed
advisable, however, in -view of the approaching SemiCentennial, to publish instead an extra number of The
Diamond, for the purpose of affording more complete
and satisfactory information for the brethren than they
could otherwise gain. Accordingly this supplement has
been issued containing full accounts of all the pro
ceedings and directions for the guidance of those who
expect to be present. By thus definitely presenting-fco
the Fraternity the arrangements which have been made
for the various exercises and for the accommodation
of the guests, it is hoped that there may be secured a
very full attendance and thereby a most successful
and notably brilliant Convention. We have taken
this means of informing all tlie brothers in re
gard to the details of the fiftieth anniversary of our
Fraternity. It will remind them of the prosperity of
our organization and will again awaken their interest
-
by giving them a knowledge of the affairs of our
brotherhood. We hope that every graduate who c in
possibly come will be present ; for it will give encour-
-
agement to the younger members and render the Con
vention more successful, enjoyable and illustrious.
A copy of this supplement ivill be sent to every
member of the Fraternity.
HEADQUARTERS.
Tlie Committee have hired four large parlors at the
Delavan to be used as
"
Headquarters"- for all the Psi
U's at the Convention. This will afford a pleasant
place for the exchange of greetings and social chats.
Committee rooms can also be procured adjoining these
apartments�
a great convenience.
As soon as the Brothers arrive in the city they will
please go immediately to the Delavan, which is across
the street from the depot. There upon inquiry they
will find the headquarters on the second floor of the
hotel. Donotmakeamistakeandgotothe "Stanwix,"
which is also very near the depot. The latter hotel is
at the end of the depot, while the Delavan is at tlie
side.
HOTEL ACCOMMODATIONS.
Hotel accommodations can be procured at the
Delavan for $2, 00, $2.50 and |3.00, the regular charges
being %^,. 00 per day.
Inasmuch as the Legislature will not then be iu ses
sion, the proprietor has consented to make the above
reduction for every one who registers W. T.
Those who attended the Convention at Syracuse will
remember that in that city no reduction could be pro
cured.
EARLY ARRIVAL.
It is earnestly requested that the brothers arrive in
Albany by Wednesday morning or as early as possible
on that day. Matters of much importance will be con
sidered in the early business meetings and a full at
tendance is most desirable. The historical meeting
also on Wednesday evening will be of peculiar interest
and value ; and it would be eminently unwise to be ab
sent on that occasion.

CONVENTION SUPPLEMENT.
APKIL OF THE FEATEENITY YEAE L.
The D1.A.MOND, a journal devoted to the interests, advancement,
and welfare of the Psi Upsilon, is issued eiiery two months, and is
designed both,for circulation among the Chapters, and for tlie infor
mation of the graduate sons of Psi Upsilon in regard to the progress
of the Fraternity.
The subscription is one dollar per annum, in advance.
All contributions, subscriptions, and communications, .should be
addressed :
THE DIAMOND,
Look Box 5T, Schenectady, N. Y.
BOARD OF EDITORS :
Henry C. Wood, Dow Beekman,
Geo. p. Allison, Wallace T. Foote.
The Committee of Arrangements for the Convention
are as follows ^ Prof. I. B. Price, Henry C. Wood,
W. M. Gilbert, bow Beekman, Geo. F. Allison, H. F.
DePuy. All communications should be sent to one
of the above.
THE DIAMOND.
This suiaplement will reach a great many Psi U's
who have never seen The Diamond, the present offi
cial organ of the Fraternity. Such we would inform
that The Diamond was established two years ago, is
a sixteen page journal, and is dependent for its sup
port upon the members of the Fraternity. We hope
that many who will see this ,
supplement will be in
duced to testify their love for Psi U. by sending us a
subscription.
The Diamond contains all the news of the Frater
nity, and through the Chapter letters which are pub
lished in every number, gives every member an idea
of just what is taking place in his college. The Dia
mond thus answers the purpose of both a
society and
college paper. The subscription per year is onedollar, and this small sum will certainly not be begrudged
by any good Psi U. , and at the same time it will aid
us very much in presenting a journal worthy of the
organization which we represent.
The full account of the Convention, together with
the literary productions of the celebrated participants,
wUl be published in The Diamond after the Conven
tion, and hence that number alone will be worth the
l^rice of subscription.
All the best Fraternities now have their society
journal and their members give their liberal support.
We trust that our graduates will be full as generous
and enthusiastic in this matter as their rivals are.
We need your subscriptions. Subscribe for The
Diamond.
BUSINESS MEETINGS.
The flrst meeting will be held at 10:30 o'clock a. m.,
Wednesday. There will be a short session in the after
noon and the succeeding meetings will then, of course,
be determined hj adjournment. The Committee
have succeeded in procuring the Court of Appeals
Chamber in the old Capitol.
THE HISTORICAL MEETING,
An unusual, yet highly attractive, feature of the
exercises will be a Historical Meeting to be held
Wednesday evening. May 23d, in tlie Old Capitol.
Prof. Willard Fiske of Cornell University, and
Albert P. Jacobs of Detroit, will present historical
sketches of the Fraternity upon "that occasion. Prof.
Fiske has been, for many years, closely identified with
the existence of the Fraternity. He is the author of
Blbliographica Psi Upsilonica, the most valuable
of recent Fraternity publications. His previous suc
cessful efforts in behalf of Psi Upsilon, and present
active interest in her welfare, give promise of a pro
duction of deep interest. Albert P. Jacobs is the
author of the first book ever published on secret societias, a zealous member of the Detroit Psi Upsilon
Alumni Association, and a brother thoroughly ac
quainted with the history of Psi Upsilon. His effort
will, undoubtedly, be a valuable feature of the exer
cises.
Several of the founders have signified their inten
tion to be present and during the evening will relate
their recollections of the oiigin and early progress of
the society. These addresses, together with those
given by the brothers actively connected with the early
existence and foundation of the Chapters, will furnish
an evening of rare enjoyment and information. No
pains will be spared to make this meeting one oii the
most memorable and instructive ones in the annals of
Psi Upsilon.
LITERARY EXERCISES.
Ex-Governor Alexander H. Eice, of Massachusetts,
will be the President of the Convention and will preside
at the Literary Exercises, which will be held in the
Leland Opera House on the evening of May 24. Bro.
Eice is one of the most noted men of whom the Fra
ternity boasts, and his presence will add much to the
Convention. He has shown in various ways his in
terest in Psi U. , having been the associate founder of
the Psi and Alpha and President of the Convention of
'77 held with the Xi.
Senator Joseph E. Hawley who will deliver the ora
tion is one of the most polished of American orators
and reflects much honor upon the Fraternity. Sena
tor Hawley has officiated in a like capacity at three
preceding Conventions and is an appropriate selection
for the 50th anniversary.

THE DIAMOND. O
Charles Dudley Warner has done us the honor to
accept the office of essayist. The fame and genius
of this author will give to the Convention a
celebrity
which will be the pride of the Fraternity. He was
the orator at the Convention of '64 held with the Psi,
and essayist at the Convention of '80 held at the Phi.
The poet, Prof. Hjalmar H. Boyesen, so noted in
letters by his charming productions, will make a val
uable contribution to Psi Upsilon literature. Prof.
Boyesen was the poet of the Convention of '77, and his
writings elicit the admiration of every one and espec
ially of Psi U's.
Prof. Calvin S. Harrington, prominent in the col
lege world, has kindly consented to write the ode for
the occasion. Bro. Harrington has graced our collec
tion of songs with several sparkling gems which are
the delight of all lovers of music.
Eev. Samuel Goodale, one of the founders of the
Fraternity, will act as chaplain and invoke the blessings
of Providence upon the order which he labored to
establish.
By reference to the list it will be seen that all who
are to take part in the exercises have heretofore on
all occasions shown themselves to be zealous and en
thusiastic Psi U's. It is to men of this character that
the Fraternity owes its prosperity and dignity.
BANQUET.
Preparations are being made which give promise of
one of the most elegant and systematically arranged
banquets ever given at any Convention.
It will be held at the Delavan House, one of the
best hotels in the State. The same hotel will, be ad
mirably suited for the headquarters of the members.
In consideration of the event we have decided that a
httle additional expense at the banquet will not be
noticed by those who attend the Convention with
the expectation of having the best of everything�
and
of paying for it.
The supper tickets are $4.00; wine tickets, extra,
$3.00. For this amount of money there can be no
possible lack of anything. The Banquet is one of
the most pleasant and enjoyable features of a Conven
tion and the committee are endeavoring to make it a
grand success.
Judging from the letters we have received and from
the general interest manifested, there will be no less
than 250 present to surround the festive board. We
hope that every Psi U. who has a spark of love for
his Fraternity left will be present at the "general
convocation," A large number of prominent mem
bers will be present to respond to toasts. With so
notable a man as Judge Hooper C. Van Vorst to pre
side, dignity wOl be added to the jollity of the occa
sion. The committee have not yet determined whether
it will be advisable to assign toasts to the undergrad
uates. The duty of responding is often considered
unpleasant by the undergraduates, and their brilliant
and eloquent remarks are not often justly (?) appre
ciated by the elder hearers.
In order to place the Banquet upon a business
basis and insure the committee against loss, we have
decided upon the following arrangement : All those
who expect to attend the Banquet must send ,$4.00
for their ticket before May 18. The wine tickets may
be procured at Albany upon arrival. If by some ac
cident a member who has procured his ticket, should
not be able to attend, the money of course will be re
funded. It is necessary that we should learn as
early
as possible how many will be present, for owing to
the large number who will attend, it would be impos
sible for us to make an estimate with any accuracy.
The proprietor of the Delavan -will set the date
when he must know exactly how' many people he will
be obliged to serve. If we should guarantee him a
certain number and should be disappointed, a loss of
money would result. We hope the brothers will
strictly observe this regulation and thereby oblige the
committee and also avoid any trouble which they
might experience by not having procured their ticket
in advjince.
Please send the money to Dow Beekman, Schenec
tady, N. Y., box 375, and your ticket \vill be returned
immediately.
THE RECEPTION.
Immediately upon the close of the literary exercises
in the Leland Opera House, carriages will be in waiting
to convey the guests to Bleecker HaU, on Broadway,
where the receiatioii wiU be held. This hall is large
and well arranged, being used entirely for occasions
of this kind. The parlors, cloak rooms, etc., con
nected with it are most convenient and perfectly
adapted for an assemblage of such size and brilliancy.
The decoration will be of great beauty. Nothing will
be overlooked which can tend to the comfort and
pleasure of the guests.
Some prominent Albany gentlemen, members of the
Fraternity, will act in conjunction with the Theta Chajjter as a reception committee, and under their supervis
ion it is impossible that the evening should be other
than one of great enjoyment.
After the promenade and presentations, dancing will
begin and continue tiU a late hour. The music will
be furnished by one of the finest and best known
bands in the state. Calling ont as it -will the most
charming and aristocratic ladies, not only of Albany
and Schenectady, but other cities many miles away,
the reception will be an event which would of itself
alone amply repay one for a most extended journey.

CONVENTION ODE.
The Convention Ode, written by Prof. C. S. Har
rington, is published in the Supplement so as to en
able the Brothers who expect to be present to become
parfectly familiar with it. It should be sung with
great effect, and a rousing chorus of hearty Psi U,
voices brought in. The song is composed to the air
"March of the Men of Harlech." The music is ex
cellent, and will bear all the voices that can be put
upon it.
Delegates, do not forget the importance of prepar
ing yourselves in this ode.

SINGING.
The singing of the Psi U. songs at the Public Ex
ercises is always an
interestingand entertainingelement
of the programme. The Committee has deemed it
advisable to announce at this early date, what songs
Avill be sung at the Public Exercises, and in order to
insure that they may be appropriately and harmo
niously rendered, earnestly requests all the Brothers
who expect to be present to assiduously practice them.
The songs selected are : Brothers, the day is ended,
Eeunion JubUee, College Chorus.
Song slips, such as have been used at previous con^
ventions, will be widely distributed, containing the fol
lowing songs : Convention Ode; Dear Old Shrine;
College Chorus; Psi U. Beer; Heartfelt Bond; Anthem;
Jolly Psi U. ; Brothers, the Dayis ended ; , The Maiden
Fair; Eeunion Jubilee; Carmen Animi ; Convention
Song. We think that this selection includes all of
our most popular songs, and trust the Brothers will
come so well drilled in rendering these songs, that the
singing will constitute a
veiy striking and enjoyable
feature of the proceedings.
DELEGATES
The Committee earnestly requests all the Chapters
to send the names of their delegates before May 18.
